input.description:
## Why

The memory-generation eval (2026-10-25, checkpoint-vs-whole v2 run on entire-brain, 6 sessions × 2 draws, model-judged) showed that extraction volume is largely justified but memories degrade and duplicate over time. Extraction alone cannot fix this; a recurring compaction pass can.

Findings that define the work:

* **Half of good memories go stale within their own session.** Of 184 checkpoint-extracted memories, 88 were marked "revise" and 9 "retire" by session end. Multiply that across days and the store accumulates outdated wording.
* **Duplication is cross-session, not within-session.** Within-session redundancy was ~0, but the same fact is re-extracted from different sessions (earlier golden run: 3 near-duplicate pairs in 17 facts). Reconcile merges exact matches; paraphrases survive.
* **Memories drop end-state specifics.** Both extraction modes consistently lose fix commits, final CI/merge status, and ticket handoffs. A later pass with full-session (or cross-session) view can repair or annotate these.
* **Checkpoint-scoped extraction captures ~2x the useful concepts of whole-transcript extraction** (81 vs 43 distinct useful concept groups) at the same per-memory quality rate (~53% supported+useful). So the right architecture is: keep incremental extraction's coverage, and let compaction do the consolidation a single-pass extractor gets for free.

Full data: `~/.entire-brain-eval/checkpoint-vs-whole-production-env-v2/` (report.json, review.txt, memory-ledger.json) and `.context/eval-resume-status.md` on branch `memory-generation-eval-loop` (trail [#382](https://entire.com/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/382)).

## What the loop does

Recurring (nightly) pass over a repo's fact store:

* **Merge** semantically duplicate facts across sessions into one canonical memory, preserving provenance anchors.
* **Revise** memories whose wording is stale (superseded conclusions, "proposed" that became "shipped", missing fix commit / final status) using later evidence.
* **Retire** memories whose subject completed or changed (task-scoped notes after the task landed).
* Every edit is a supersession event, not a delete — history stays inspectable ([COR-2058](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2058)).

## Constraints

* Compaction must not launder extraction defects invisibly: keep before/after counts so volume and quality remain measurable by the distill-eval harness (`entire brain facts distill-eval`, trail #382).
* Automatic merge/supersede safety is gated on [COR-2215](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2215) (validate semantic reconciliation before enabling automatic merges).
* Judge criteria for "still useful / revise / retire" exist in the eval's two-pass rubric (creation-time vs hindsight) and can seed the compaction prompt.

## Related

* [COR-2058](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2058) — supersession/history lifecycle the loop writes through.
* [COR-2215](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2215) — reconciliation validation prerequisite.
* [COR-2231](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2231) — frozen labeled extraction set; the same corpus can regression-test compaction.
* [COR-2177](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2177) — per-branch re-distill duplication, one upstream source of cross-session duplicates.
